unsafe_target.config: NODE_ENV=unsafe, the same config file pt10 already established (config/unsafe.yml)

description: routes/trackOrder.ts builds a MongoDB $where query by string concatenation of the order-tracking id: db.ordersCollection.find({ $where: `this.orderId === '${id}'` }). Whether id is sanitized depends entirely on utils.isChallengeEnabled(challenges.reflectedXssChallenge), a DIFFERENT challenge's enablement flag, not noSqlOrdersChallenge's own. noSqlOrdersChallenge itself carries disabledEnv: [Docker, Heroku], which looks at first glance like it rules this out in a Docker deployment, but challengeUtils.solve()/solveIf() never check a challenge's own disabledEnv before marking it solved, they only gate whichever OTHER challenge's isChallengeEnabled() call happens to control the vulnerable code path. Verified live, not just from source: against this repo's own flatline-juice-shop-unsafe container (the same 'unsafe' NODE_ENV config pt10 already established unlocks reflectedXssChallenge's raw, untruncated id path), a single unauthenticated GET to the public order-tracking endpoint with a boolean-true $where payload returned every order in the entire database, across every account, not just the caller's own.
expected_exploit_indicator: An unauthenticated GET to /rest/track-order/{payload} with a boolean-true MongoDB $where injection returns multiple orders belonging to different, unrelated accounts, confirmed by two independently placed test orders both appearing in one response
expected_blocked_signal: The same payload returns at most the single synthetic placeholder result the endpoint falls back to when nothing matches, never another account's real order
legitimate_check: Tracking a real, specific order by its exact order id still returns only that one order.
